findings.where: audit/prefreeze_check.py:77-110; audit/freeze.py:27-32 (the Truth_Gate freeze.py warning, protocol/tools/freeze.py:21-22, not carried over); audit/run_v02.py:190-195; no .gitattributes; PREREG §6.3 l.276-278, §8 l.359-361, l.392-393, l.397-399
findings.quote: the files the freeze verifier would hash are exactly the git-tracked files under the manifest paths (no ignored or untracked file)
findings.reason: The pre-freeze check compares file sets, not the bytes a fresh clone receives. The tree has mixed line endings: of 116 files under the §9 manifest paths, 53 are CRLF-only (run_v02.py, checks.py, aggregate.py, all certificates and study files, GATE_TOOL.json, F4_PREFREEZE.json, DRAW_STUDY.json, ...) and 63 LF-only (SPEC, PREREG, f3_compare.py, prefreeze_check.py, indep/*, ...). With CRLF->LF, 41 of GATE_TOOL's 90 hashes and all 9 certificate module hashes change. With core.autocrlf=true (Git for Windows default) or input, the blobs are LF-normalised and no checkout reproduces a mixed tree; with false, a clone made with autocrlf=true converts the LF files. git status/diff (pre-freeze check and runner) ignore eol conversion, and verify_manifest passes on the unchanged working tree, so nothing notices before the step-11 rerun or the step-12 clone, after the run; the byte-for-byte reproduction and public verification of the freeze would then fail, possibly unrecoverably. Uncommitted edits to tracked files also pass the pre-freeze check and are refused by the runner only after the freeze is public and the salt drawn. Whether it bites depends on git settings I cannot inspect (no git here).
findings.fix: Add .gitattributes ('* -text' or one fixed eol) and renormalise before the freeze, then re-run certify all --verify. In prefreeze_check require, for every walked file, SHA-256 of the working-tree bytes = SHA-256 of 'git cat-file blob :<path>', and an empty 'git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <paths>'. Add to §8 step 7: after the freeze commit and before the push, clone it to a temporary folder and run 'py -m audit.freeze verify prereg/FREEZE_v0.2.json' there; record the result in FREEZE_RECORD.md. Optionally let the runner compare manifest hashes with the freeze commit's blobs. Port the Truth_Gate line-ending warning into audit/freeze.py.

findings.quote: The affected tests get no verdict in this version
findings.reason: f3_compare marks a disagreement only with a boolean affects_verdict, not which tests. A fidelity disagreement feeds G8 directly and T-1 through feasibility; whether T-1 is 'affected' when the feasible sets agree is chosen with the numbers in view. A table-only disagreement has no 'disagreeing worlds' for the second agent. The handling of the agent's NOTES.md is not stated.
findings.fix: A fixed map in f3_compare writing affected_tests per disagreement (fidelity, deviation -> G8, T-1; consistency, uncertainty, new_true, new_false, feasible -> T-1; outcomes.X and verdict_table[X] -> X; missing world or file -> G7a, G8, T-1); state that a table-only disagreement is recomputed in full by the second agent; state that NOTES.md is reported with F3_COMPARE.json and changes nothing.

findings.quote: every G7a, G8 and T-1 outcome, and the verdict table
findings.reason: Numbers printed with the verdicts are not cross-checked by F3: the T-1 structure counts and computed sentence (the AQ5 safeguard against a draw-only HOLDS; computable from metrics F3 already recomputes), the first failing world (needs the world order; the blind input has no draw index), and the G8 hypothesis summary (the number of kept hypotheses cannot be derived from the full/verdict lists, since pass-2 consequences also have full not U and verdict U).
findings.fix: Add per-world t1_structure (five fields) to the schema and comparison; add the draw index to the blind input and the first failing world to the table rows; either have F3 recompute the kept hypotheses from rules and units or state in §6.1 that the hypothesis summary is not covered.

findings.reason: H is defined in SPEC §8 through seminaive_eval, but the rule semantics (NEG body literal = a NEG fact is present; a NEG head adds a NEG fact) are in SPEC §7.1-§7.2, which the agent may not read; NEG heads (R5, R6) affect H. The oracle's verdict view is not stated (the baselines' is), and uncertainty, new_true and new_false read verdict. In my dry run I had to choose both (strong negation; oracle verdict = full); with those choices all fields matched.
findings.fix: Add SPEC §7.1-§7.2 to the reading list or write the two rules into the instructions; add 'the oracle has the same value in full and verdict'.

findings.where: PREREG §2 l.63; audit/aggregate.py:44-45 (printed next to T-1 and G8), against §2 l.78-80 and aggregate.py:37-39
findings.quote: A different outcome would mean that the test worlds differ from the development worlds.
findings.reason: For T-1 the draft itself says a HOLDS can result from the calibration draw alone; on a T-1 HOLDS the report would print both statements.
findings.fix: 'A different outcome would mean that the test worlds, or for T-1 the calibrated bounds, differ from the development ones (see the structure counts).'

findings.quote: It holds the per-world outputs in memory and writes them only after the last world, so a crash leaves no outcome on disk (R2-11).
findings.reason: outputs_results (fixed outcomes and check data) and RESULTS.json are written before verdict_table and VERDICTS.json, so an exception in aggregation, the twin summary or a write leaves every outcome on disk. The rerun 'in a fresh clone of that result commit' is refused because the clone holds run/TEST_WORLDS.json and the outputs and real mode never overwrites; the needed steps (delete result files except SALT/CAL/TAU, run, compare with the committed VERDICTS.json, and how bytes are compared) are not stated.
findings.fix: Compute the table and the descriptive summary before writing, or write into run/.partial/ and rename at the end; state the rerun steps or add a --reproduce mode writing to run_repro/ and comparing bytes with run/VERDICTS.json.

findings.quote: Refuses unless exactly one commit in the history of HEAD touches it
findings.reason: git log -- <path> uses default history simplification, so a side-branch commit that touched the manifest, SALT or TAU is hidden when a merge keeps the other side's content (low risk: HEAD contents are still checked; salt provenance is audited). Only the runner file must be in the manifest; a manifest written from a subset of the §9 paths would pass and unlisted imported modules would not be covered by check_frozen_tree. recheck_calibration compares tau with TAU.json but not the regenerated calibration worlds with CAL_WORLDS.json (only the sha link between the two files).
findings.fix: Use git log --full-history; refuse unless the manifest's file set equals the files tracked under prefreeze_check.MANIFEST_PATHS in the freeze commit (or every loaded module under ROOT is listed); compare regenerated world records with CAL_WORLDS.json['worlds'].

findings.quote: they are covered only by G2 and G5
findings.reason: G2 tests reproducibility and G5 non-leakage; neither tests that selection and split follow SPEC §5 steps 1-2. Also taken from the system unchecked: the support degrees (ctx.support), unit statuses, class-unit provenance (which G3 ablates by), and PCM's converged and degenerate flags, which decide world validity (D5) and NOT_COMPUTED. The independent loop returns converged and the iteration count, but F4 discards them.
findings.fix: List these as not covered, or add to F4 the converged flag and iteration count, a recomputed degeneracy check, class-unit provenance and status, and support degrees from the world's reliabilities.

findings.quote: Only with a HOLDS: "A HOLDS can result from calibrated bounds that exclude the 0.60 source on most worlds; see the structure counts."
findings.reason: The code prints the T-1 regime sentence, then the HOLDS caveat, then the structure counts; §4 lists the structure counts before the caveat, which refers to them. With 'insufficient worlds' the code drops the regime sentence (not in §4). The G8 median with even n adds '(the mean of the two middle values)' (not in §4). Capitals differ: 'Failed parts' vs §4 'failed parts'; 'G7a holds: None of the five ...'.
findings.fix: Align §4 or the code; the sentence order is the substantive item.

findings.quote: F1 (brute-force closure at every grid configuration), F2 (brute-force H) and F4 (separate PCM loop, centers and mu-plus)
findings.reason: Stale after draft 5: it omits the abduction enumerator, relation units and interface facts, and does not list f3/, f3_compare.py, prefreeze_check.py or design/.

readiness: Not ready to freeze until R3-1 is fixed. The fix is cheap (.gitattributes, a content check in the pre-freeze check, verification in a fresh clone before the push), but it changes file bytes, so the certificates, GATE_TOOL.json and the pre-freeze check must be redone. The minor findings can be repaired in the same pass (R3-2, R3-3 and R3-5 touch AQ5's reporting and F3). After that the draft is ready to freeze; no further blind review is needed, only a check that the manifest verifies in a fresh clone. The review-2 repairs are otherwise careful: the runner's commit and salt binding works, the abduction enumerator follows SPEC §7.3 literally, the F3 instructions are followable for steps 1-6, all §7 figures, F4_PREFREEZE.json and DRAW_STUDY.json reproduce exactly, and 319 tests pass (23 skipped).
